journal_lines: Wedged between two roots: a ring of worked §lbone§r and river-iron. §oSmelled of copper and old soil. Brought it home.
Something fashioned, not formed. Bone bent into a circle, wire twisted to hold it. Carried it carefully.
Half-buried at the base of a dead tree. §oThe smell was old in a way that made the ears go flat. Took it anyway.
The crown was sized for a head smaller than mine. Did not think too long about whose.
Bone and antler, wired with copper green from age. §oThe craftsmanship was deliberate. The maker had patience.
Whoever last wore it did not come back for it. The roots had started to grow through.
Set it down to look at it properly. Picked it up again. Neither felt like a choice.
Old enough that the bone had taken the color of the earth around it. Still unmistakably made.
